title: Rigid sphere in a viscoelastic elastomer: stiffness vs bulk modulus, displacement vs mixed u-p (frequency response, analytic)
description:
Kelvin's rigid spherical inclusion in a compressible viscoelastic solid, and volumetric locking of the displacement formulation. A rigid sphere of radius a = 1 um is moved by X = 1 nm along the axis inside a concentric held sphere r = b = 5 a filled with an elastomer: G*(w) = G0 (1 + j eta) + G1 j w tau1 / (1 + j w tau1), K* = kappa G0 (1 + j eta) (shear_modulus G0 = 0.5 MPa, one shear Prony branch G1 = 1.5 MPa, tau1 = 1 ms (relaxation around 1 / (2 pi tau1) = 159 Hz), mechanical_loss_factor eta = 0.05 on G0 and K0, rho = 1000 kg/m^3), frequency_response at 6 log-spaced frequencies 10 Hz - 3 kHz, swept over kappa = K0 / G0 = 1, 10, ..., 1e5 (PDMS-like elastomers have kappa ~ 1e3 - 1e4). Axisymmetric (r, z), m = 0, P2 triangles (h = a/8 on the sphere, growth 1.25, a/2 at most: 1019 triangles). Half model: only z > 0 is drawn; a translation along z has u_z even and u_r odd in z, so the plane z = 0 (y_lo) holds u_r = 0 with u_z free (displacement feature 'plane', u_y empty; sigma_zz = 0 there is natural) and the drawn half carries half the force: the derived values double F_y. The sphere ('inclusion', prescribed_displacement_domain u_y = X) and everything outside r = b ('wall' = window minus the cavity, fixed_domain: every node of its elements, so the sphere r = b is clamped) have their own material 'held' (another parameter group, so in the mixed formulation the pressure is duplicated on r = a and r = b and the held regions, where div u = 0, do not drag the elastomer pressure there toward 0: with the elastomer's own values the mixed error at kappa = 1 rises from 1.2e-5 to 2.5e-3).
One model, both formulations: two solid_mechanics physics on the same mesh with the same features, 'disp' (formulation displacement, P2) and 'mixed' (Taylor-Hood P2 / P1 u-p); every run solves both.
Analytic (quasi-static elasticity with complex moduli by the correspondence principle; nu = (3 K - 2 G) / (2 (3 K + G)) complex): u = F(r) e_z + H(r) (e_z . r_hat) r_hat is a sum of the four l = 1 Navier solutions (F, H) = (1, 0) (translation), ((3 - 4 nu) / r, 1 / r) (Kelvin), (1 / r^3, -3 / r^3) (dipole) and (r^2, -2 (2 - 3 nu) r^2 / (3 - 2 nu)) (regular); u = X e_z at r = a and u = 0 at r = b give a 4 x 4 system. Only the Kelvin term carries a net force (P = 16 pi G (1 - nu) C_Kelvin; the others are force-free), so with t = a / b, S = 1 + t + t^2 + t^3 + t^4 and q = K* / G*(w) the force the support exerts on the sphere is F = 12 pi a X G* (3 q + 4) (3 q + 10) S / ((1 - t) (2 (3 q + 10) (6 q + 11) S - 5 t (1 + t)^2 (3 q + 1)^2)) (= minus the force of the elastomer on the sphere). b -> inf: Kelvin's 12 pi G a X (3 q + 4) / (6 q + 11) = 24 pi G a X (1 - nu) / (5 - 6 nu) (6 pi G a X incompressible); q -> inf: the Stokes sphere-in-a-sphere wall factor 4 S / ((1 - t)^3 (4 + 7 t + 4 t^2)) (Haberman-Sayre / Happel-Brenner; 1.756 at t = 0.2). The Kelvin far field decays like 1 / r, so a container changes the force at O(a / b) without screening: here by x1.27 - 1.30 (kappa = 1) to x1.74 - 1.76 (kappa >= 1e3), which is why the reference keeps the container exactly. Checked independently of the FEM: symbolic Navier residual of each basis field, the two limits above, and the traction integrals over r = a and r = b of the numerically assembled solution (complex G, K) equal to the closed form to 1e-8. Inertia is left out of the reference: (k_s b)^2 = rho w^2 b^2 / |G*| <= 4.4e-6 at 3 kHz, and runs with rho x 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 shift F at 3 kHz by -9.3e-5, -9.3e-4, -9.3e-3 (linear in rho): -9e-8 at rho = 1000; the sphere's own inertia rho a^2 w^2 / (9 |G*|) < 2e-8.
Curves & tables tab: the support reaction of 'inclusion' of each physics (F_y_re, F_y_im of the drawn half) versus frequency with their analytic curves (per sweep value): the stiffening and the loss peak of the Prony branch. Sweep tab: mixed_stiffness_10Hz and disp_stiffness_10Hz = 2 Re F / (6 pi G0 a X) (the relaxed modulus, where K* / G* is largest) versus kappa against the dashed closed form (1.086 at kappa = 1 to 1.777 at 1e5). Derived values tab: the stiffness at 10 Hz and 3 kHz and the loss tangent Im F / Re F at 98 Hz (0.62 - 0.76), the mixed ones graded, the displacement ones reported only (their error is the locking). Derived curves tab: locking_ratio = Re F_disp / Re F_mixed per frequency at the last kappa (1e5). Field tab (kappa = 1e5, 3 kHz): mixed.u_y, mixed.pressure (the pressure unknown) and disp.pressure (-tr(sigma*) / 3, node-averaged).
Measured agreement (this mesh): mixed |F - F_ref| / |F_ref| = 1.1e-5 (kappa = 1) to 2.3e-5 (kappa >= 1e3) at every frequency, whatever kappa (the derived values 2.3e-5, the loss tangent 4.7e-6, the curves 3.1e-5 of their range); tolerances 1e-4. Displacement formulation at 10 Hz: 1.7e-5, 6.3e-5, 2.3e-4, 8.2e-4, 3.7e-3, 1.6e-2 for kappa = 1 ... 1e5 (7.8e-2 at 1e6, not swept): about kappa^0.65, too stiff, and smaller at 3 kHz (6.8e-3 at 1e5) where |G*| is 4x larger, so the locking parameter is K* / G*(w), not K0 / G0. Mesh study (h on the sphere a/4, a/8, a/16, a/32, largest triangle 4x that), |F - F_ref| / |F_ref| at kappa = 1e4, 10 Hz: mixed 1.7e-4, 2.3e-5, 3.2e-6, 5.4e-7 (~h^2.8, the same at 1e5), displacement 2.4e-2, 3.7e-3, 5.3e-4, 9.1e-5 (at 1e5, a/8 - a/32: 1.6e-2, 2.6e-3, 4.6e-4): P2 converges at the same rate but with an error constant that grows with kappa, roughly 160x (1e4) to 700x (1e5) the mixed one, so near-incompressible solids need the mixed formulation (or a mesh refined by a factor that grows with kappa). To see locking in another model: switch formulation from mixed to displacement and raise bulk_modulus.
